messages:
sara: Heads up — after the 02:00 runtime roll we're seeing a p99 jump for short text-only decode paths. p50 stable. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/roll-2005 :grimacing:

miguel: I pulled the perf dump. Prefix cache hit-rate for short prompts dropped from ~74% -> ~39% over the last 45m. Request mix hasn't changed much. Suspect interaction between continuous-batching composition and the new keying path.

devon: Repro'd on staging. Attached profiler excerpt (trimmed):
```
batch_window_ms: 10 -> avg_batch_size: 6.2 -> singletons: 28%
avg_queue_ms: 3.8
prefix_cache_hit: 41%
latency_p50: 11ms p99: 156ms
```
Notably, batch composition now frequently mixes very short seqs (<=16) with midsize (<=128). When mixed, KV cache lookup is low.

lia: Quick hypothesis: cache key canonicalization changed in the rollout. The continuous-batcher adds padding tokens before kernel selection / serialization; the key we compute used the post-pad buffer instead of the original trimmed prompt. So identical prompts hashed to different keys depending on batch placement.

miguel: Bingo. I diffed the keying code. New kernel-selection path runs `serialize_kv_v2()` which includes sequence-length in the hash blob. Old path used `normalize_prompt()` before hashing. When grouped in a batch, the sequence-length field is the max seq in that batch -> key differs.

bench-bot: alert: regression-detection triggered: prefix_cache_hit_rate < 50% for short_prompts (service: rl-runtime). Ticket: RD-INC-2342.

sara: For immediate mitigation we can either: 1) normalize keys pre-batch (cheap), 2) bias continuous-batcher to form like-length cohorts (affects throughput), or 3) disable the new serialize_kv_v2 until we fix. Which do folks prefer for the canary?

devon: Short-term: normalize keys pre-batch. Patch idea: compute `prefix_key = sha256(trim_trailing_whitespace(prompt) + canonicalize_unicode(prompt))` before any padding or kernel-driven metadata is appended. That keeps keys invariant to batch composition.

lia: I ran a micro-experiment:
- baseline (pre-roll): hit=74% p99=120ms
- roll (no fix): hit=39% p99=198ms
- patch (normalize pre-batch): hit=69% p99=132ms
Tradeoff: small extra CPU to canonicalize, but latency improvement >> keeping old regression.

miguel: Also noted an interaction with kernel selection: the new fused attention kernel changes memory layout so we had to switch to `serialize_kv_v2` claiming better compactness. If we keep pre-batch normalization, we can safely keep v2 and get the kernel benefits. But we should add a serialization-version flag to avoid accidental future regressions.

sara: Action items:
- devon -> PR with pre-batch canonical keying + unit tests for invariance (RD-PR-4117) [ETA 2h]
- lia -> run canary with normalized keys on 10% of traffic and collect hit/latency for 1h (RD-CAN-89) [ETA 3h]
- miguel -> add a regression test that runs mixed-length continuous-batcher workload and asserts zero-key-drift across batch placements (RD-TST-509) [ETA tomorrow]
- ops -> hold rollback unless canary fails hard :thumbsup:

devon: I'll include a small fuzz test that generates same prompt but inserts in different batch positions and asserts identical prefix_key. Example snippet in PR: 
```
for pos in [0, mid, end]:
  batch = insert_prompt_at(prompts, pos)
  keys.append(compute_prefix_key(batch[pos].text))
assert all(k == keys[0] for k in keys)
```

lia: Also adding a perf-monitor probe to track `prefix_key_version` and `batch_composition` labels in the traces so we can roll up by kernel selection.

sara: Thanks team. If canary confirms, we'll ship to prod tonight and follow up with a small postmortem note.

miguel: One last note — this class of bug (serialization coupled to batch-time metadata) should be added to our perf-regress checklist. I'll file a short doc.

bench-bot: note: RD-CAN-89 created; RD-PR-4117 opened (link in ticket).
